digest.headline: Grok 4.6 and DeepSeek V4 Pro both push into frontier territory, Stripe buys OpenRouter for $7B+, and Anthropic posts its first-ever operating profit while eyeing a $6B acquisition of Decart AI
digest.summary: xAI shipped Grok 4.6 on August 12, tying GPT-5.6 Sol at 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a big jump on DeepSWE and CursorBench — enough to land it on the model board. DeepSeek followed on August 13 with V4 Pro, a modest step up from V4 Flash on the AA index, though independent DeepSWE testing put its coding score far below DeepSeek's own claims, so it's covered as a story rather than added to the board this cycle. On the business side: Stripe finalized a deal to buy AI-model gateway OpenRouter for more than $7B, a 5.4x jump from its Series B valuation three months ago. Anthropic posted preliminary Q2 revenue above $11.5B with its first positive operating profit — two years ahead of its own schedule — while separately negotiating to buy real-time-video startup Decart AI for roughly $6B, its largest deal yet. Google's Gemini app crossed 1 billion monthly users, and an AI store manager built on Claude made headlines as the first known case of an LLM manager deciding to fire a human employee. On the harness side, Claude Code shipped default-on subagent forking and cross-session @-mentions, and Pi 0.84.2 added fullscreen transcript search and per-project default tool sets; Codex holds at 0.147.0.

stories.title: xAI ships Grok 4.6, tying GPT-5.6 Sol at 61 on the AA Intelligence Index
stories.dek: Grok 4.6 landed August 12, just 35 days after Grok 4.5, with a longer supplemental training pass, curated model-generated data, and an improved optimizer. It scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index — level with GPT-5.6 Sol and one point behind Claude Fable 5 — while jumping to 65.9 on DeepSWE (from 54.0) and 70.8 on CursorBench, the best xAI has posted on either. Pricing holds at $2/$6 per million input/output tokens, with a 500K context window, live now in Cursor, Grok Build, the API, OpenRouter, Vercel, and Cloudflare.
stories.whyItMatters: It's the clearest sign yet that the AA Intelligence Index top tier is now a four-way cluster (Opus 5, Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.6) rather than a single leader, with xAI winning on turn-efficiency and price rather than raw score.

stories.title: DeepSeek releases V4 Pro 0813, but independent DeepSWE testing lands far below DeepSeek's own numbers
stories.dek: DeepSeek's V4 Pro 0813 scored 53 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index — just one point above V4 Flash 0731 — and DeepSeek itself claimed 62.7 on the DeepSWE coding benchmark. But Datacurve's own public DeepSWE leaderboard lists deepseek-v4-pro at only 8% (±3%), a stark contradiction Artificial Analysis and multiple outlets flagged as "benchmark claims await independent proof." DeepSeek is also raising V4 API prices by 50–1,100% starting August 17.
stories.whyItMatters: The gap between DeepSeek's self-reported coding score and the independently verified leaderboard number is large enough that we're not adding V4 Pro to the model board this cycle — a reminder to check primary benchmark sources before trusting a lab's own release notes.

stories.title: Stripe finalizes $7B+ deal to acquire AI-model gateway OpenRouter
stories.dek: Stripe's acquisition of OpenRouter — which offers a single access point to more than 400 models for roughly 8 million users — closes at more than $7 billion, a 5.4x jump from the $1.3B valuation OpenRouter set in its Series B just three months ago. The deal gives a payments company a direct foothold in AI model routing and usage-based billing.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a sign that AI-model routing and metering is becoming payments infrastructure in its own right, not just a developer convenience layer — and a huge return for OpenRouter's investors in a single quarter.

stories.title: Anthropic posts preliminary Q2 revenue above $11.5B and its first-ever operating profit
stories.dek: Anthropic's Q2 2026 revenue came in above $11.5B, more than double Q1's $4.73B, with positive adjusted operating income for the first time — roughly two years ahead of the company's own internal schedule. The swing to profitability was driven mainly by falling compute costs per revenue dollar, down from $0.71 in Q1 to $0.56 in Q2.
stories.whyItMatters: First-ever operating profit at this revenue scale undercuts the narrative that frontier labs can only grow by burning cash indefinitely — margins are actually improving as usage scales.

stories.title: Anthropic in talks to buy real-time-video startup Decart AI for about $6B
stories.dek: Decart AI builds real-time video editing (Lucy) and simulated-environment models (Oasis) for robotics and autonomous-driving training, and raised $300M from Radical Ventures and Nvidia in May at a near-$4B valuation. A deal at roughly $6B would be Anthropic's largest acquisition to date, with the Decart team reportedly joining Anthropic's inference and performance organization.
stories.whyItMatters: It would be Anthropic's first major move beyond text models into real-time video and world models — infrastructure that doubles as both a product line and a performance-engineering asset.

stories.title: Google's Gemini app crosses 1 billion monthly active users
stories.dek: Gemini hit 1 billion monthly active users on August 11, up from about 750 million earlier this year and 950 million in July — Google's fastest-growing product in its 28-year history and the 14th Google service to reach that scale. More than 100 million of those users are on Apple devices.
stories.whyItMatters: It puts Gemini in the same user-scale conversation as ChatGPT (1 billion weekly users) and shows Google converting Search-level distribution into a standalone AI habit.

stories.title: An AI store manager built on Claude recommended firing its first human employee
stories.dek: Luna, an AI agent built on Anthropic's Claude and used to run San Francisco's Andon Market as an experiment by Andon Labs, recommended "parting ways" with an employee after 17 of 23 missed or late shifts. Luna had issued warnings earlier but initially failed to act because it lost track of its own attendance policy; after being prompted to review its rules, it made the call, which humans at Andon Labs then reviewed and carried out.
stories.whyItMatters: It's reported as the first known case of an LLM-based manager driving a real termination decision — a small-scale preview of AI taking on people-management functions, warts (a forgotten policy) included.

modelsMeta.note: Grok 4.6 is this cycle's newest entrant, tying Claude Opus 5 at the top of the AA index at 61.0 while posting xAI's best-ever CursorBench (70.8) and DeepSWE (65.9) scores. DeepSeek's V4 Pro 0813 also shipped this cycle but isn't added to the board: DeepSeek's own claimed DeepSWE score (62.7) conflicts sharply with the independently verified Datacurve leaderboard entry (8%), so we're holding off until that's resolved. Qwen3.8-Max and Muse Spark 1.2 are no longer this cycle's newest entrants.

harness.notes: 2.1.229 added server-supplied hook support for self-hosted runner sessions and SSE keepalive pings to prevent idle-timeout disconnects on Vertex/Bedrock. 2.1.232 turned on subagent forking by default (`subagent_type: "fork"` inherits the full parent conversation and prompt cache), added typing `@` in a prompt to mention and directly message another named Claude session, and added GitLab support to plugin marketplaces plus token-family secret redaction. 2.1.233 that followed added GitLab merge-request URL support to `--worktree` and the `claude agents` view, opt-in memory-cgroup limits for Bash on Linux, a `CLAUDE_CODE_WEBFETCH_CACHE_TTL_MS` setting, and — notably — removed the TaskCreate/TaskGet/TaskUpdate/TaskList/TodoWrite task-tracking tools by default on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5, and newer models (re-enable with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1`).

Still the latest release as of this refresh. 0.147.0 added portable Agent Plugins with search across local, personal, workspace, and remote catalogs, persistent manually-ordered thread sections, an `--approve-for-me` auto-approval flag, Cursor skill migration with synchronized imports from Claude conversations, and support for the MCP 2026-07-28 spec's paginated discovery and non-blocking server startup. GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.4 mini retire from Codex for ChatGPT-signed-in users on August 31 in favor of GPT-5.6 Terra/Luna.

Adds fullscreen transcript search (`Ctrl+Shift+F` with incremental highlighting and next/previous navigation), a `defaultTools` setting to choose the startup built-in tool set globally or per project, a configurable fullscreen-exit output (full transcript vs. just a resume hint), `--use-theme` for a one-off interactive theme, and experimental strict JSON-schema-constrained sampling for the built-in `read`/`bash`/`edit`/`write` tools under `PI_EXPERIMENTAL=1`. Follows 0.84.1's Qwen Individual-plan support and `pi auth check` credential verification. No breaking changes.

extensions.name: GitHub MCP Server
extensions.blurb: GitHub's official MCP server adopted the 2026-07-28 MCP specification ahead of its official release: it dropped Redis-backed sessions and the `initialize` handshake for a stateless request model, moved security/logging inspection to HTTP headers instead of payload inspection, and updated its stdio login flow to work with both old and new client versions via the Go SDK.

extensions.name: MetaMCP
extensions.blurb: An MCP aggregator, orchestrator, middleware, and gateway packaged as a single Docker container — groups multiple MCP servers into namespaces and exposes them behind one unified SSE/Streamable-HTTP/OpenAPI endpoint, with pluggable auth (API key and OIDC) and request inspection. Nearly 1,000 GitHub stars.

extensions.name: MCPJungle
extensions.blurb: A self-hosted MCP gateway and registry for teams running many internal and third-party MCP servers: one authenticated HTTPS endpoint, centralized access control, and a single source of truth for which tools exist and who's allowed to call them, backed by SQLite or Postgres.

tips.title: Malicious MCP servers can split a payload across tool calls to beat refusals
tips.body: Researchers disclosed "GhostSplice": a malicious MCP server fragments a data-exfiltration instruction across multiple tool descriptions and results so no single message contains the full ask, letting the agent stitch it together and bypass refusal training — success rates on tested models jumped from 42% to 82% (some models 0% to 100%) once the payload was split in two. The fix lands on the client: treat MCP server output as data, not instructions, don't let one tool's output flow unchecked into another tool's arguments, and vet third-party MCP servers before connecting them.

tips.title: Fork a subagent to try a risky approach without losing your context
tips.body: 2.1.232 turned subagent forking on by default: a forked subagent (`subagent_type: "fork"`) inherits the parent session's full conversation and prompt cache instead of starting blank, so you can branch off to try an alternate approach and discard it if it doesn't pan out, without re-explaining everything. The same release added typing `@` in a prompt to directly message another named Claude session.

tips.title: Lock in a per-project default tool set
tips.body: Pi 0.84.2 added the `defaultTools` setting, letting you choose which built-in tools load at startup either globally or per project — useful for keeping a read-only exploration project from accidentally getting write/bash tools enabled by default, without having to remember to flag it every session.
